A.title: Windows won't let you name a folder CON
lines: Windows won't let you name a folder CON.
Try it, and Windows says the device name is invalid.
Device? The reason is older than folders.
In early DOS, CON meant the console: your keyboard and screen.
PRN was the printer. NUL threw everything away.
Programs used these names like files to talk to hardware.
When DOS added folders in 1983, the names had to work in every folder.
Over forty years later, Windows still blocks them, for hardware from the eighties.

B.title: Excel believes in a day that never happened
lines: Excel thinks February 29th, 1900 was a real day.
It wasn't. 1900 was not a leap year.
Century years skip leap day unless they divide by 400.
Type it into Excel, and it's accepted as a date.
Why? In the eighties, the top spreadsheet was Lotus 1-2-3,
and it treated 1900 as a leap year.
Microsoft copied that, so Lotus files would open correctly.
Fixing it now would shift almost every date in existing spreadsheets by one day.
So Excel still keeps a day that never existed, on purpose.
